newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian PM sees EMU deal at Amsterdam summit.
newsitem.headline: Belgian PM sees EMU deal at Amsterdam summit.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said on Friday he expected European Union leaders to reach a deal on economic and monetary union (EMU) and on a review of the EU internal workings, dubbed the IGC, at next week's Amsterdam summit.
Speaking after the weekly cabinet meeting he also said he expected the summit to produce a deal on the coordination of economic policy and job creation in Europe.
"Contrary to reports earlier this week I think it will be possible to agree on the single currency and the IGC," he said.

"Nobody is questioning EMU itself or the stability pact as such. We will, however, talk about coordination of economic policies, notably in the realm of employment. I hope that besides the stability pact we will also be able to approve a text about the coordination of economic policy."

Asked whether he thought the Amsterdam summit could fail, Dehaene said, "We will only have certainty when the agreement has been signed, but meanwhile all the contacts I have had indicate that everybody wants to reach an agreement."

Asked whether the Amsterdam summit could set numerical criteria for job creation such as the Maastricht Treaty sets for, for instance, state finances and inflation, he said, "I do not think that it would make sense to introduce criteria in the same way."
"It is important that the EU help orientate economic policy, but nobody disputes that job creation is a national responsibility," Dehaene said.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6810, Fax +32 2 230 7710
